volume: Vol. I: The Age of Crucible & Cipher
description: Before the establishment of peer-reviewed journals, natural knowledge was encoded in alchemical anagrams, astrological ephemerides, and private correspondence between princely patrons.
Gravitation, calculus disputes, the standardization of pendulum clocks, and the earliest vacuum experiments that shook Aristotelian physics.
The isolation of invisible airs: dephlogisticated gas, inflammable air, fixed air, and the chemical revolution that unfolded against the backdrop of the French Terror.

volume: Vol. IV: The Steam & Specimen Empire
description: Global botanical plunder, railway thermodynamics, telegraph cables across ocean trenches, and the earliest geological discoveries that pushed Earth's age into the deep abyss.

volume: Vol. V: The Invisible Germ & Cell
description: The fierce resistance to antisepsis, the invention of aniline dyes that stained invisible cellular organelles, and the birth of epidemiological mapping in cholera-stricken cities.

volume: Vol. VI: The Disintegration of Matter
description: X-rays burning photographic plates in dark drawers, glowing radium salt tubes, the discovery of the electron, and the shattering of classical deterministic physics.

volume: Vol. VII: The Laboratory of the State
description: Radar, synthetic penicillin mass manufacture, the Manhattan Project, codebreaking machines at Bletchley, and the agonizing moral bargains of wartime science.

volume: Vol. VIII: The Code of Life & The Cosmos
description: Photograph 51, radio telescopes listening to pulsars, plate tectonics verified across mid-ocean ridges, and the race to decipher the genetic alphabet.
Ice core drilling in Antarctica documenting historical atmospheres, polymerase chain reactions, the human genome project, and the dawn of computational simulation.

volume: Vol. X: The Anthropocene & The Algorithm
description: CRISPR gene editing in living embryos, gravitational wave detectors with laser interferometers, deep learning unrolling protein folding, and space telescopes observing early galaxies.
